title: Tidal to ban and remove millions of AI-generated tracks as AI slop inundates music streaming
lede: Tidal will start deleting fully AI-generated songs on December 9 and refuse new ones, after AI tracks made up more than 43% of its uploads over the past 90 days.

points: More than 29 million songs should be gone by year end, and Tidal expects to reject 80,000 to 85,000 tracks a day.
Distributors may no longer deliver fully AI-generated tracks, and metadata marking a song as wholly AI-made means rejection.
Songs made with AI assistance are still accepted.
Tidal counts 27 million fully AI tracks, 6.3% of its catalog, and says 96% of them have no streams.
Demonetizing AI tracks from June failed to slow uploads, according to Tidal Music's lead.

sections.text: Tidal's line runs through detection and upload metadata, so how an AI-assisted track is declared now decides whether it ships. Deezer is adding a filter toggle, while Spotify and YouTube Music only label.
